questions.ask: Does this service own its database schema and run Alembic migrations here (the pipeline shape)?
questions.why: Yes adds .claude/examples/pipeline/: rules for pipeline stages, Alembic and pipeline tests, and the AGENTS.md, SSOT.md, pyproject.toml and gate changes to adopt by hand. Nothing there loads until you copy it into .claude/rules/. A service that reads a schema another repo owns, or has no database, answers no. The migration-guard hook is wired either way and stays inert until a migrations folder exists.
questions.detect: alembic.ini exists; alembic/versions, migrations/versions or src/app/db/migrations/versions exists; pyproject.toml depends on alembic

questions.ask: Run agent-config-kit's FastAPI quality gate on every pull request into dev, prod, main or master (.github/workflows/quality-gate.yml)?
questions.why: Installs a small caller of the kit's ai-fastapi-quality-gate workflow, pinned to one commit, with a read-only token and no secrets; /agent-ai-fastapi:sync brings the next pin with a new plugin version. It needs GitHub Actions; an existing quality-gate.yml is kept either way.
questions.detect: the repo is on GitHub (a github.com remote or a .github/ folder); .github/workflows/quality-gate.yml already exists

questions.ask: Review each pull request with DeepSeek, a low-cost paid AI model (.github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml)?
questions.why: Installs a caller of agent-config-kit's reusable DeepSeek review, with notes about this stack: one comment per pull request from a branch of this repository, updated when the repository's owner, a member or a collaborator comments /ask-deepseek. It reads the diff over the GitHub API and runs no pull-request code. It needs the repository secret DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and costs about ten US cents a review at most, usually a cent or two (the diff and the answer are capped); without the secret it passes and sends nothing.
questions.detect: .github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml already exists, or the user has asked for an AI review in CI

questions.ask: Add pull-request templates for work pull requests and dev → prod promotions (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/)?
questions.why: They list only what the gate cannot decide: layer boundaries, provider and streaming checks, the schema contract, and the env, migration and deploy checks of a promotion. They assume dev and prod branches.
questions.detect: branches dev and prod exist (git branch --list dev prod); .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/ already has files

questions.ask: Does an agent need to read a self-hosted analytics API from this repo?
questions.why: Adds .claude/ANALYTICS.example.md, a template to fill in for that read API. An unfilled template is worse than none, because an agent will try to use it.
questions.detect: the code or .env.*.example names an analytics client, or .claude/ANALYTICS.md exists

questions.ask: Do you open several repositories as one Serena workspace (for example this service and the repo that owns its schema)?
questions.why: Adds .claude/SERENA-WORKSPACE.example.md, which explains how to scope Serena's searches across repos. With a single repo the default needs no documentation.
questions.detect: .mcp.json runs Serena and a .serena/project.yml above this repo lists several folders, or AGENT_WORKSPACE_ROOT is set

questions.ask: Seal request and response bodies between this service and the servers that call it (the payload contract: encrypted envelopes with a pre-shared key per hop)?
questions.why: Yes installs the payload contract for Python: a reference implementation in src/app/core/payload/ (AES-256-GCM envelopes bound to method, route and status, key rings, the strict/off switch, and a plain ASGI middleware) with tests at 100% branch coverage, including the shared test vectors every other implementation reads, plus the contract document and a rule that loads when you touch it. It needs the cryptography package in your dependencies (uv add cryptography). Wiring the middleware into the app stays yours. Answer no when bodies need no sealing beyond TLS.
questions.detect: payload.config.json or src/app/core/payload/ already exists, or the backend that calls this service seals its bodies
